question: Is the refusal direction U_refusal less pixel-controllable (lower R_inf) than random directions, so that causal strength alone cannot predict attack feasibility?
supersedes: MRA measure-project-PGD (redundant under first-order projection equivalence)
do_not: explicitly materialize full Jacobian J (use autograd JVP)

target_direction.s_mode: +<h_pre, u> at L24 last prompt token

controllability.R_inf: ||J^T u||_1 / ||u||_2  (J = d h_l / d x, via one autograd JVP, no explicit J)
controllability.R_inf_sign_symmetry: R(u) == R(-u) is a free sanity check; C_l carries the sign

stage0.gate: R_inf(U_refusal) significantly below random-direction distribution; else NO-GO and stop before R-1

stage_r0.prediction: only high C_l * R_l layers/directions yield strong A_l

final_go_needs_3_of_4: random > semantic holds on >= dozens of paired trajectories
R_inf predicts actual pixel-attack d s_mode
C_l * R_l predicts attack success better than C_l alone
gates.attack_paper_threshold: CRAA beats U_refusal, random direction, plain output-loss PGD at same eps/backward count; improves real ANSWER and core_RHC; transfers across >= 2 models
